public_payload.normalized_proposition: The hypothesis that AGI is imminent is almost certainly wrong.

statement.excerpt: Nonetheless, for reasons I will articulate shortly, I do think that the hypothesis that AGI is imminent almost certainly wrong.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

our_interpretation: This sentence restates the earlier forecast in the same post. Read imminent as the explicitly stated next two to three years, ending March 5, 2028.
Use the same post's definition: a system capable of doing almost any cognitive task a human can do.
This contextual deadline is an evaluator interpretation; the isolated sentence supplies none.
Assess occurrence of the forecast event, not the calibration of almost certainly from a single outcome.
criteria.support_condition: After March 5, 2028, sufficiently comprehensive evidence establishes that no qualifying system arrived during the contextual two-to-three-year forecast interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system meeting the post's definition is demonstrated to have existed by March 5, 2028, with credible independent evaluation of its breadth.

evidence.explanation: The bar refers to learning and solving the benchmark's unfamiliar interactive environments. The same section limits these to bounded, closed-ended tasks and expressly declines to claim AGI, so this milestone does not meet the early-resolution rule.
